LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleTraditional: 一組人／物 + 都 + 動作／描述
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleEnglish: Say Both or All with 都
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Say that every person or thing in a group shares the same action or quality.
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Name the whole group first, then put 都 before what the group does or is like. 都 looks back and means “both” or “all.”

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing
ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

discoveryLab.title: Gather the group before 都
discoveryLab.description: 都 collects everyone or everything already named, then gives them one shared result.

choices.label: All people
choices.note: 我們 is the group. 都 comes before the action 買.

choices.label: Both colors
choices.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge yánsè dōu hěn hǎokàn.
choices.english: These two colors both look good.
choices.note: The two colors share the same description.

choices.label: All share “not”
choices.pinyin: Tāmen dōu bù xǐhuān hē chá.
choices.english: None of them likes drinking tea.
choices.note: 都 comes before 不 because the whole group shares the same "not".

choices.label: Repair placement
choices.traditional: 都他們喜歡 → 他們都喜歡
choices.simplified: 都他们喜欢 → 他们都喜欢
choices.pinyin: dōu tāmen xǐhuān → tāmen dōu xǐhuān
choices.note: Name the group before 都.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Group first, 都 second, shared action or description last.

patternRows.english: These two colors both look good.
None of them likes drinking tea.

items.question: Where does 都 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the whole group, before the action or describing word. Never at the start.

right.english: All of us like drinking tea.

items.question: How do I say "none of them likes tea" — 都不 or 不都?
items.answer: Put 都 before 不: 都不 means "every one does not". 不都 means "not all" — a different meaning.

items.question: Can I use 都 with just one person, like "I all like this book"?
items.answer: No. 都 needs two or more people or things. With one, drop 都.

text.traditional: 這兩件衣服都很漂亮。
text.simplified: 这两件衣服都很漂亮。
text.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu dōu hěn piàoliang.
text.english: These two items of clothing are both beautiful.

text.traditional: 我們都不要去他家。
text.simplified: 我们都不要去他家。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu bú yào qù tā jiā.
text.english: None of us wants to go to his home.

text.traditional: 他們都喜歡喝珍珠奶茶嗎？
text.simplified: 他们都喜欢喝珍珠奶茶吗？
text.pinyin: Tāmen dōu xǐhuān hē zhēnzhū nǎichá ma?
text.english: Do they all like drinking bubble milk tea?

words.meaning: ending word for a yes-or-no question

questions.repairFeedback: Keep the group together, then use 都 before 很貴.

Place 都 after the group.

LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Describe a Noun or Replace It with 的
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Describe the thing you want and avoid repeating an obvious noun.
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: Use 的 to link a describing word to a noun. With short one-syllable words, you can usually skip 的. If what you are talking about is already clear, you can drop the noun and just leave 的.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing
ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.pattern: Description + 的 + noun, or description + 的

discoveryLab.title: Keep 的 when the thing is not named
discoveryLab.description: 的 can join a describing word to a thing, or stand in for a thing everyone already knows.
discoveryLab.prompt: Does the listener need the thing named again?

choices.label: Say the noun
choices.note: A longer description uses 的 before the noun.

choices.label: Short description
choices.note: With a one-syllable description such as 新, 的 is often omitted.

choices.label: Noun already known
choices.english: He wants to buy the big one.
choices.note: 大的 keeps 的 because it stands for the thing already named.

choices.label: Do not drop both
choices.traditional: 我要買大 → 我要買大的
choices.simplified: 我要买大 → 我要买大的
choices.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi dà → wǒ yào mǎi dà de
choices.english: I want to buy the big one.
choices.note: When the thing is dropped, 的 stays.

discoveryLab.takeaway: If the thing is not named, 的 stays: 大的, 新的, 便宜的.

patternRows.english: Part 1 · inexpensive things (multi-syllable description uses 的)
Part 2 · new books (single-syllable description omits 的)
Part 3 · the big one (known noun omitted, 的 stays)

items.question: The thing is already clear. Can I drop 的 too?
items.answer: No. When the noun goes, 的 must stay: 大的, 新的.

right.english: I want to buy the big one.

words.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing

items.question: Do I need 的 between 好看 and 蛋糕?
items.answer: Yes. Longer describing words like 好看 or 可愛 take 的 before the noun.

words.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing

items.question: Short words like 小 — do they also need 的?
items.answer: No. One-syllable words like 小 or 新 drop 的: 小蛋糕, 新書.

right.english: I want to buy a small cake.

examples.teachingNote: 的 connects the multi-syllable description 快樂 to 孩子.

text.traditional: 他是一個快樂的孩子。
text.simplified: 他是一个快乐的孩子。
text.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge kuàilè de háizi.
text.english: He is a happy child.

examples.teachingNote: 可愛的孩子 keeps 的 because 可愛 has two syllables.

text.traditional: 李太太有三個可愛的孩子。
text.simplified: 李太太有三个可爱的孩子。
text.pinyin: Lǐ tàitai yǒu sān ge kě’ài de háizi.
text.english: Mrs. Li has three lovely children.

examples.teachingNote: 漂亮 takes 的 before the noun 花.

text.traditional: 我喜歡漂亮的花。
text.simplified: 我喜欢漂亮的花。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān piàoliang de huā.
text.english: I like pretty flowers.

examples.teachingNote: Single-syllable description 好 omits 的: 好朋友.

text.traditional: 你有幾個好朋友？
text.simplified: 你有几个好朋友？
text.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu jǐ ge hǎo péngyǒu?
text.english: How many good friends do you have?

examples.teachingNote: Single-syllable description 小 omits 的: 小蛋糕.

text.traditional: 我要買一個小蛋糕。
text.simplified: 我要买一个小蛋糕。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi yí ge xiǎo dàngāo.
text.english: I want to buy a small cake.

examples.teachingNote: Single-syllable description 新 omits 的: 新同學.

text.traditional: 他是我們的新同學。
text.simplified: 他是我们的新同学。
text.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen de xīn tóngxué.
text.english: He is our new classmate.

examples.teachingNote: 蛋糕 is already mentioned, so it is omitted; 的 stays: 大的, 小的.

text.traditional: A：你們要買哪個蛋糕？ B：他要買大的，我要買小的。
text.simplified: A：你们要买哪个蛋糕？ B：他要买大的，我要买小的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen yào mǎi nǎ ge dàngāo? B: Tā yào mǎi dà de, wǒ yào mǎi xiǎo de.
text.english: A: Which cake do you want to buy? B: He wants the big one; I want the small one.

examples.teachingNote: 衣服 is omitted; 便宜的 and 貴的 retain 的.

text.traditional: A：你要買哪件衣服？ B：我要買便宜的，不要買貴的。
text.simplified: A：你要买哪件衣服？ B：我要买便宜的，不要买贵的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào mǎi nǎ jiàn yīfu? B: Wǒ yào mǎi piányi de, bú yào mǎi guì de.
text.english: A: Which piece of clothing do you want to buy? B: I want to buy the cheap one, not the expensive one.

examples.teachingNote: 花 is omitted; 那朵漂亮的 retains 的.

text.traditional: A：妳想買哪朵花？ B：我想買那朵漂亮的。
text.simplified: A：你想买哪朵花？ B：我想买那朵漂亮的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xiǎng mǎi nǎ duǒ huā? B: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi nà duǒ piàoliang de.
text.english: A: Which flower would you like to buy? B: I would like to buy that pretty one.

subsections.title: Connecting Descriptions (Description + 的 + Noun)
subsections.explanation: Place 的 between a describing word and a noun, like “a pretty flower” or “a happy child.”

subsections.title: Short One-Syllable Words (Skip 的)
subsections.explanation: With common one-syllable words like 好 (good), 新 (new), or 大 (big), you can skip 的 directly, like 好朋友 (good friend) or 新書 (new book).

subsections.title: Dropping the Noun When It Is Already Known
subsections.explanation: If you and the listener already know what item you are talking about, you can leave out the noun and end with 的, like saying “I want the red one” (紅色的).

LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleTraditional: 這／那／哪 + 數量 + 名詞
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Point to This, That, or Which Thing
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Point to things that are near or far, or ask which one someone means.
LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: Start with 這, 那, or 哪, then add the number, measure word, and noun. With one item, 一 is often omitted; with two, use 兩.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing
ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

LESSON_THREE_GRAMMAR_THREE.pattern: 這 / 那 / 哪 + number + measure word + noun

discoveryLab.title: Pick the pointing word first
discoveryLab.description: The first word shows distance or asks the listener to choose.
discoveryLab.prompt: What job should the first word do?

choices.label: Near · 這
choices.note: Use 這 for something near the speaker. 一 is normally omitted here.

choices.label: Far · 那
choices.note: Use 那 for items farther away. Two becomes 兩 before 本.

choices.label: Choose · 哪
choices.note: 哪 asks the listener to choose one.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Choose 這, 那, or 哪 first, then the full number + measure word + noun.

items.question: This book is in my hand. Do I point with 這 or 那?
items.answer: 這 — it is near you. 那 is for things farther away.

items.question: I am choosing one thing to buy. Should my answer use 哪?
items.answer: No. 哪 asks "which?" in the question. Your answer chooses with 這 or 那.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi zhè zhǒng bǐ.
right.english: I would like to buy this kind of pen.

items.question: Which comes first — the pointing word or the number?
items.answer: The pointing word first: 這 / 那 / 哪, then the number, measure word, and noun.

right.pinyin: Zhè sān jiàn yīfu hěn piàoliang.

text.traditional: A：你喜歡喝哪種茶？ B：我喜歡喝這種茶。
text.simplified: A：你喜欢喝哪种茶？ B：我喜欢喝这种茶。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xǐhuān hē nǎ zhǒng chá? B: Wǒ xǐhuān hē zhè zhǒng chá.
text.english: A: Which kind of tea do you like? B: I like this kind of tea.

text.traditional: A：這四枝筆怎麼樣？ B：這四枝筆很好看。
text.simplified: A：这四枝笔怎么样？ B：这四枝笔很好看。
text.pinyin: A: Zhè sì zhī bǐ zěnmeyàng? B: Zhè sì zhī bǐ hěn hǎokàn.
text.english: A: How are these four pens? B: These four pens look good.

words.meaning: how is it; what do you think

text.traditional: A：這兩本中文書很新嗎？ B：一本很新，一本不新。
text.simplified: A：这两本中文书很新吗？ B：一本很新，一本不新。
text.pinyin: A: Zhè liǎng běn Zhōngwén shū hěn xīn ma? B: Yì běn hěn xīn, yì běn bù xīn.
text.english: A: Are these two Chinese books new? B: One is new; one is not.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe a Noun or Replace It with 的
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe the thing you want and avoid repeating an obvious noun.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 的 to link a describing word to a noun. With short one-syllable words, you can usually skip 的. If what you are talking about is already clear, you can drop the noun and just leave 的.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing
ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

grammarPages.pattern: Description + 的 + noun, or description + 的

discoveryLab.title: Keep 的 when the thing is not named
discoveryLab.description: 的 can join a describing word to a thing, or stand in for a thing everyone already knows.
discoveryLab.prompt: Does the listener need the thing named again?

choices.label: Say the noun
choices.note: A longer description uses 的 before the noun.

choices.label: Short description
choices.note: With a one-syllable description such as 新, 的 is often omitted.

choices.label: Noun already known
choices.english: He wants to buy the big one.
choices.note: 大的 keeps 的 because it stands for the thing already named.

choices.label: Do not drop both
choices.traditional: 我要買大 → 我要買大的
choices.simplified: 我要买大 → 我要买大的
choices.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi dà → wǒ yào mǎi dà de
choices.english: I want to buy the big one.
choices.note: When the thing is dropped, 的 stays.

discoveryLab.takeaway: If the thing is not named, 的 stays: 大的, 新的, 便宜的.

patternRows.english: Part 1 · inexpensive things (multi-syllable description uses 的)
Part 2 · new books (single-syllable description omits 的)
Part 3 · the big one (known noun omitted, 的 stays)

items.question: The thing is already clear. Can I drop 的 too?
items.answer: No. When the noun goes, 的 must stay: 大的, 新的.

right.english: I want to buy the big one.

words.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing

items.question: Do I need 的 between 好看 and 蛋糕?
items.answer: Yes. Longer describing words like 好看 or 可愛 take 的 before the noun.

words.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing

items.question: Short words like 小 — do they also need 的?
items.answer: No. One-syllable words like 小 or 新 drop 的: 小蛋糕, 新書.

right.english: I want to buy a small cake.

examples.teachingNote: 的 connects the multi-syllable description 快樂 to 孩子.

text.traditional: 他是一個快樂的孩子。
text.simplified: 他是一个快乐的孩子。
text.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge kuàilè de háizi.
text.english: He is a happy child.

examples.teachingNote: 可愛的孩子 keeps 的 because 可愛 has two syllables.

text.traditional: 李太太有三個可愛的孩子。
text.simplified: 李太太有三个可爱的孩子。
text.pinyin: Lǐ tàitai yǒu sān ge kě’ài de háizi.
text.english: Mrs. Li has three lovely children.

examples.teachingNote: 漂亮 takes 的 before the noun 花.

text.traditional: 我喜歡漂亮的花。
text.simplified: 我喜欢漂亮的花。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān piàoliang de huā.
text.english: I like pretty flowers.

examples.teachingNote: Single-syllable description 好 omits 的: 好朋友.

text.traditional: 你有幾個好朋友？
text.simplified: 你有几个好朋友？
text.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu jǐ ge hǎo péngyǒu?
text.english: How many good friends do you have?

examples.teachingNote: Single-syllable description 小 omits 的: 小蛋糕.

text.traditional: 我要買一個小蛋糕。
text.simplified: 我要买一个小蛋糕。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi yí ge xiǎo dàngāo.
text.english: I want to buy a small cake.

examples.teachingNote: Single-syllable description 新 omits 的: 新同學.

text.traditional: 他是我們的新同學。
text.simplified: 他是我们的新同学。
text.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen de xīn tóngxué.
text.english: He is our new classmate.

examples.teachingNote: 蛋糕 is already mentioned, so it is omitted; 的 stays: 大的, 小的.

text.traditional: A：你們要買哪個蛋糕？ B：他要買大的，我要買小的。
text.simplified: A：你们要买哪个蛋糕？ B：他要买大的，我要买小的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen yào mǎi nǎ ge dàngāo? B: Tā yào mǎi dà de, wǒ yào mǎi xiǎo de.
text.english: A: Which cake do you want to buy? B: He wants the big one; I want the small one.

examples.teachingNote: 衣服 is omitted; 便宜的 and 貴的 retain 的.

text.traditional: A：你要買哪件衣服？ B：我要買便宜的，不要買貴的。
text.simplified: A：你要买哪件衣服？ B：我要买便宜的，不要买贵的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào mǎi nǎ jiàn yīfu? B: Wǒ yào mǎi piányi de, bú yào mǎi guì de.
text.english: A: Which piece of clothing do you want to buy? B: I want to buy the cheap one, not the expensive one.

examples.teachingNote: 花 is omitted; 那朵漂亮的 retains 的.

text.traditional: A：妳想買哪朵花？ B：我想買那朵漂亮的。
text.simplified: A：你想买哪朵花？ B：我想买那朵漂亮的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xiǎng mǎi nǎ duǒ huā? B: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi nà duǒ piàoliang de.
text.english: A: Which flower would you like to buy? B: I would like to buy that pretty one.

subsections.title: Connecting Descriptions (Description + 的 + Noun)
subsections.explanation: Place 的 between a describing word and a noun, like “a pretty flower” or “a happy child.”

subsections.title: Short One-Syllable Words (Skip 的)
subsections.explanation: With common one-syllable words like 好 (good), 新 (new), or 大 (big), you can skip 的 directly, like 好朋友 (good friend) or 新書 (new book).

subsections.title: Dropping the Noun When It Is Already Known
subsections.explanation: If you and the listener already know what item you are talking about, you can leave out the noun and end with 的, like saying “I want the red one” (紅色的).

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 一組人／物 + 都 + 動作／描述
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say Both or All with 都
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that every person or thing in a group shares the same action or quality.
grammarPages.explanation: Name the whole group first, then put 都 before what the group does or is like. 都 looks back and means “both” or “all.”

discoveryLab.title: Gather the group before 都
discoveryLab.description: 都 collects everyone or everything already named, then gives them one shared result.

choices.label: All people
choices.note: 我們 is the group. 都 comes before the action 買.

choices.label: Both colors
choices.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge yánsè dōu hěn hǎokàn.
choices.english: These two colors both look good.
choices.note: The two colors share the same description.

choices.label: All share “not”
choices.pinyin: Tāmen dōu bù xǐhuān hē chá.
choices.english: None of them likes drinking tea.
choices.note: 都 comes before 不 because the whole group shares the same "not".

choices.traditional: 都他們喜歡 → 他們都喜歡
choices.simplified: 都他们喜欢 → 他们都喜欢

choices.note: Name the group before 都.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Group first, 都 second, shared action or description last.

patternRows.english: These two colors both look good.
None of them likes drinking tea.

items.question: Where does 都 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the whole group, before the action or describing word. Never at the start.

right.english: All of us like drinking tea.

items.question: How do I say "none of them likes tea" — 都不 or 不都?
items.answer: Put 都 before 不: 都不 means "every one does not". 不都 means "not all" — a different meaning.

items.question: Can I use 都 with just one person, like "I all like this book"?
items.answer: No. 都 needs two or more people or things. With one, drop 都.

text.english: These two items of clothing are both beautiful.
